solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Long to join circle and express view

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearning to join a discussion group so they can air their opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, so it means to express a view.

clue.text: Boss, old member, glowers among disciples?

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
haloes are the glowing rings painted round the heads of the saints and disciples, so they are what glows among them

explanation.surface: A boss, once a party member, scowls at his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glowers' is not a scowler but a thing that glows: the halo of a saint. The question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An omphalos is a central boss or knob, such as the raised centre of a shield; the word is Greek for navel.

clue.text: Understanding current things differently

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: arranged differently, so the letters of the word things are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Grasping modern matters in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' reads as 'present-day' in the surface, but it is physics shorthand; 'differently' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding of a person or situation, a near synonym.

clue.text: Satanic force to be coming from below

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word coming up from below is read bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: The devil's power is rising up from the pit below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from below' reverses LIVE, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is the wicked power personified by Satan, the force of wickedness.

clue.text: Shell ready to take over an experimental facility

indicators.note: to take something over here means to take it in, so the money word holds the other pieces

parts.note: ready money, readies, is cash
an gives the article A
a lab is a laboratory where experiments are done

explanation.surface: A company shell with funds ready to buy out a research laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests a shell company; it is the definition, a gourd shell. 'to take over' puts ALAB inside CASH, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd whose hard dried shell is used as a bowl or bottle.

clue.text: Nurse at work with pains located round sick body part

indicators.note: placed around, so the pains word encloses the sick word

parts.note: aches are pains
ill means sick
to nurse is to tend
on means working, operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A nurse on duty deals with aches surrounding a damaged part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'located round' signals the container; the clue gives the second word's pieces first, so the charade is assembled out of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The tendon joining calf muscle to heel bone is a part of the human anatomy.

clue.text: Macho man unable to open desk

indicators.note: without its opening, so the first letter of the name is lost

parts.note: Rambo is the musclebound hero of the Sylvester Stallone films

explanation.surface: A tough guy who cannot get his desk open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unable to open' drops the first letter from RAMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early Christian churches.

clue.text: Hunter in exploit over long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means written above the next piece

parts.note: an exploit is a deed, an act
an aeon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: A hunter engaged in a single feat across a lengthy stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon in Greek myth was a huntsman turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: Problem for couple

definitions.meaning: to couple is to hook together, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: A difficulty facing two people together.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a problem, and attaching one thing to another couples them, as also does getting married informally.

clue.text: Composer's gravity risks no upset

definitions.note: read as 'Composer is', the apostrophe s acting as a link

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer's seriousness never takes chances on causing offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky was the Russian-born creator of The Rite of Spring, a major twentieth-century composer.

clue.text: Pack animal in tack before grand departure

indicators.note: in puts the animal inside the tack word

parts.note: a tack is a small pin
an ass carries packs
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A donkey kitted out in harness ahead of a grand exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tack' looks like horse harness but is a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing is a gentle word for death, a departure from this life.

clue.text: Sailor interrupting assassination at home

indicators.note: breaking into, so the sailor sits inside the killing word

parts.note: a hit is a contract killing
AB, able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor intervening in a murder plot at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a creature lives, its home.

clue.text: Bark associated with golden retriever?

parts.note: a bark (barque) is a ship; the ship of Jason, who went to retrieve the Golden Fleece, not a dog's woof

explanation.surface: A dog's woof linked to a golden retriever breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all dogs; 'Bark' is a sailing vessel and the 'golden retriever' Jason, fetching the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Charge having caught river fish

indicators.note: caught means holding, so the charge word encloses the river letter

parts.note: a toll is a fee charged for using a road or bridge
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fee for having landed a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is a verb here, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: Fourth man went down hard

parts.note: the sun set, went down
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The fourth man in a line-up took a heavy fall.
explanation.walkthrough: After Adam, Cain and Abel, Seth is the fourth man named in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth, the third son of Adam, is the fourth male person in the Bible's account.

clue.text: Erica has no longer to conserve energy

indicators.note: conserving means keeping, so the old verb holds the energy letter

parts.note: hath is the archaic form of has, no longer used
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A woman called Erica no longer has the strength to save her energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erica' looks like a woman's name; it is the botanical genus of heathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heathers, low shrubs also called heath.

clue.text: Southern runner, sometimes in form, gets cut

parts.note: a hare is a fast runner that rests in a form, a hollow in the grass

explanation.surface: A southern athlete, at times on top form, gets dropped from the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' sounds like an athlete's good spell, but a form is a hare's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A share is a portion, as in a cut of the profits.

clue.text: End for development with Horton Heath as alternative

indicators.note: up for development, like land to be rebuilt, so these letters are remodelled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A site's end use is earmarked for building, with Horton Heath, a Hampshire village, as the other option.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a contrasting point, offering the alternative view.

clue.text: Strong man in Lima captivated by womanly signals?

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman

indicators.note: held captive by, so the letter for Lima sits inside the signals

parts.note: cues are signals to act
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A muscleman in Peru's capital is charmed by a woman's suggestive hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lima' is not the Peruvian city but the radio code for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules is the mythic hero famous for his strength, a byword for a strongman.

clue.text: Get cross in game

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it
to bridge a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: Getting angry in the middle of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the verb to span.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard modern form of the card game played by four in partnerships.

clue.text: Busy hospital in Eton botched attempt

indicators.note: in puts the hospital letter inside the jumbled word
botched means bungled, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: H is the road-sign abbreviation for hospital
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: A busy sanatorium at Eton College makes a bungled try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges ETON into ONTE, and 'in' places H inside it. Eton is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Being constantly active and moving about is a common idiom for being busy.

clue.text: Muscle produced when old diet changes

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Muscle is built when someone changes their old eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The deltoid is the triangular muscle covering the shoulder joint.

clue.text: Singer in market releasing right single

indicators.note: letting go of, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the Rialto in Venice is a famous market district
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A singer at a market releases a record that is right for single release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' takes R and I from RIALTO, the Venetian market by the famous bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range below soprano.

clue.text: Great British king swallowed bitter

indicators.note: swallowed means taken in, so the king letter goes inside

parts.note: ace means excellent, great
R from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A great British monarch downed something sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' puts R inside ACE B, just before the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare word for sour or harsh in taste or temper, the same sense as acerbic.

clue.text: Food item with rocket served first

indicators.note: placed in front, so the rocket comes before the other piece

parts.note: the V-1 was a German wartime flying bomb, written V1 and read as VI
and means together with

explanation.surface: A dish with rocket salad leaves served as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket' looks like the salad leaf; it is the V-1 flying bomb, with 1 read as Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an article of food, an old literary word usually met in the plural.

clue.text: Alliance formed when bar not closed

indicators.note: with its closing letter left off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to block is to bar

explanation.surface: A partnership formed when a pub refuses to shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but means obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties combined for a common purpose, an alliance.

clue.text: Reveal secret national symbol in conversation

indicators.note: spoken in conversation, so the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the leek is the national emblem of Wales

explanation.surface: Letting slip a country's emblem during a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is worn by the Welsh on St David's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: To leak information is to disclose it without authority, to let out a secret.

clue.text: Advance slowly under His roof?

parts.note: under a roof is in a building, so under gives in
His, with the capital, is God; His roof is the church, abbreviated CH

explanation.surface: Moving forward cautiously while lodging in some man's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Under His roof means in church: IN CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward by tiny degrees, very slowly.

clue.text: English indeed catching the French unsighted?

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the affirmation encloses the French article

parts.note: yes and indeed both affirm
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: An Englishman indeed catches the French napping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' signals the container; 'the French' is the plural article of French, not a French person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking eyes leaves one without sight; the question mark admits unsighted is a stretch.

clue.text: Self-inflicted damage to have end

parts.note: to own is to have
a goal is an end, an aim

explanation.surface: Harming yourself just to reach a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A football score against your own side is used figuratively for any act that harms its doer.

clue.text: Bear left, reaching westerly city borough

parts.note: to brook is to bear, tolerate

indicators.note: heading west, i.e. right to left in an across clue, so the city is read backwards

parts.note: NY, New York City

explanation.surface: A bear turned left, arriving at a city district out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: Such a descent involves underworld

indicators.note: the phrase involves, contains, the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: That kind of descent takes one down to the realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek realm of the dead, ruled by the god of that name.
